name: Indeterminate Word

dimensions.form: Closed series sharing historical wh- orthography (how included); internal paradigm structure (whose, whom as case forms of who); productive -ever derivation
dimensions.meaning: Contributes an open variable restricted to a sort (person, thing, selection, possessor, place, time, reason, manner/degree)
dimensions.function: Feeds interrogative, relative, and exclamative packagings; the marked property percolates upward, with non-subject fronting where the packaging requires it
dimensions.distribution: Availability and lexical category vary by member and packaging; non-subject phrases are fronted in the relevant constructions

1.definition: Contributes an open variable restricted to a sort, available to different clause-type packagings
1.details: Term: indeterminate (cf. Kuroda 1965 for the Japanese analogue). Not a CGEL lexical category: the set cross-cuts lexical categories, and category may differ by packaging and function—interrogative what is a determinative in determiner use (what size) but a pronoun when it heads an NP (What did you see?), whereas exclamative what is an adjective; how is adverbial. Three projections support the overarching set: (i) sortal-variable semantics across packagings; (ii) upward percolation of the interrogative, relative, or exclamative property, plus non-subject fronting where required; (iii) the -ever series (whoever, whatever, whichever, wherever, whenever, however) derives from this base set. Packaging-specific category facts live in the specialization entries and lexicon layer.

examples.note: Open variable over things (fused relative packaging)

2.definition: Marks scalar degree, a point or extent on an implicit or explicit scale
2.details: Degree is one of the sorts the series ranges over

relatedConstructions.notes: Deitality status varies by packaging: ignorance-reading fused relatives pattern deitally; free-choice readings are mixed; exclamative uses are non-deital (Reynolds, deitality inventory)

grounds.note: Indeterminate as the term for the analogous Japanese series

projection.target: The same sortal form can occur in what Jo wrote after admire or wonder. With admire, the expression can denote an entity or text. With wonder, it presents an open question. The lexical shape does not determine the packaging.
projection.evidence: CGEL compares matching clause-like strings across fused relatives and embedded interrogatives and gives independent agreement and distributional tests.

curious.title: The who, what, where family of words
curious.summary: Words like who, what, where, when, why and how share one job, which is to stand for something left open, and different sentence types put them to different uses.
curious.body: Who, what, which, where, when, why and how all leave something open. Who leaves open a person, where a place, when a time. This dictionary calls them indeterminates, and the same word can serve a question, a relative phrase or an exclamation. Compare what she saw with who came. In what she saw, the word stands for a thing. In who came, it stands for a person, and the sentence asks which one. Words ending in ever, such as whoever and whenever, come from the same set. Degree belongs here too: how tall asks about a point on a scale.
curious.try: Take who, where and when. What kind of thing does each one leave open?

teacher.summary: Gives the overarching idea behind wh-words across questions, relatives and exclamatives, and warns they don't form one word category.
teacher.explain: This dictionary treats who, whom, whose, what, which, where, when, why and how, plus the -ever series, as one set whose members contribute an open variable restricted to a sort: person, thing, selection, possessor, place, time, reason, manner or degree. The set isn't a CGEL lexical category, because it cross-cuts categories. Interrogative what is a determinative in what size but a pronoun when it heads an NP, as in What did you see?; exclamative what is an adjective; how is adverbial. The same form can occur in what Jo wrote after admire or wonder: after admire it can denote an entity or text, and after wonder it presents an open question. The lexical shape doesn't determine the clause type. This analysis is provisional.
teacher.terms: Textbooks sometimes call the interrogative uses wh-words or question words. This dictionary's term for the wider set, which also covers relative and exclamative uses and the -ever series, is indeterminate.

contrasts.note: Can denote an entity or text; compare the next line.

watch_for: A learner might assume that who, what and how all belong to one word class in CGEL, though this dictionary says the set cross-cuts classes.
A learner might assume a form such as what has one category in every use, though interrogative what is a determinative in what size and a pronoun in What did you see?
teacher.activity: Give sentences with what, who, where and how in questions, relatives and exclamations. Students sort the uses by clause type and name the kind of thing each word leaves open.

checked.note: Fixed: teacher.watch_for no longer presents what size and What did you see? as a change of clause type (both are interrogative; they illustrate category differing by function); teacher.terms now limits wh-word and question word to the interrogative uses and says the dictionary's set is wider; replaced 'the entry' with 'this dictionary'.
